concerns.text: Task T028 implements 'Phylogenetic Signal-Adjusted Spearman' for N < 30. The spec (FR-004) mandates 'Phylogenetic Generalized Least Squares (PGLS)' for all correlation analysis. The plan (Phase 2) introduced this substitution, but the task list fails to document this as a sanctioned exception or requirement amendment, creating a silent weakening of the FR-004 constraint.

Task T029 implements 'Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) FDR' as the primary method. The spec (FR-005) mandates 'permutation-based FDR correction (or Benjamini-Yekutieli)'. While the plan (Phase 2) substituted BH, the task list does not explicitly link this deviation to a documented exception or requirement amendment, violating the constraint that tasks must not silently relax spec demands.

FR-009 requires the system to 'fallback to species-level aggregation analysis' if linkage fails. Tasks T020 and T031 implement the logic to aggregate and output a 'Descriptive Case Study' report. However, there is no task to re-run the statistical analysis pipeline (US2) on the aggregated data. This silently narrows the FR-009 requirement from a functional fallback analysis to a mere descriptive report, violating the acceptance criteria of US1/US2.

Task T039 hardcodes a numerical equivalence tolerance of '1e-6'. The spec (SC-003) requires equivalence 'within a tolerance of a sufficiently small threshold'. Hardcoding a specific value without a mechanism to validate its appropriateness for the specific floating-point operations (PGLS/Spearman) constitutes a silent narrowing of the acceptance criterion, risking false failures or false passes.

Task T057 implements a pre-filtering step to remove features present in < 10% of isolates. The spec (FR-007) requires retaining 'ALL features where the adjusted p-value < 0.05' in the raw output. Pre-filtering before analysis risks removing valid significant features that are rare, contradicting the requirement to report all significant features in the raw output, unless explicitly documented as a sanctioned exception.
